en: When the night comes with its breezes and its shadows to console the scorched earth, and all of nature rests, the slave goes to water with his sweat and his tears the enclosure where the night has no shadows, nor the breeze freshness: because there the fire of the firewood has replaced the fire of the sun, and the unhappy black, turning without ceasing around the machine that extracts its sweet juice from the cane, and the metal boilers in which this juice is converted into honey by the action of the fire, sees hour after hour pass, and the sun that returns finds him still there... en: "What then!" he cried with a choked voice; "does Carlota love that man so much?"
draft: "What then!" he cried with a choked voice; "does Carlota love that man so much?"
adequacy: "What then!" he cried with a choked voice; "does Carlota love that man so much?"

es: -Tanto -respondió Teresa-, que acaso no sobreviviría a la pérdida de su amor.

draft: "So much," replied Teresa, "that perhaps she would not survive the loss of his love.
adequacy: "So much," replied Teresa, "that perhaps she would not survive the loss of his love.

es: ¡Sab! -prosiguió con voz llena y firme, si es cierto que amas a Carlota con ese amor santo, inmenso, que me has pintado; si tu corazón es verdaderamente capaz de sentirlo; desecha para siempre un pensamiento inspirado únicamente por los celos y el egoísmo.
en: Sab!" she continued with a full and firm voice, "if it is true that you love Carlota with that holy, immense love that you have described to me; if your heart is truly capable of feeling it; cast aside forever a thought inspired solely by jealousy and selfishness.
draft: Sab!" she continued with a full and firm voice, "if it is true that you love Carlota with that holy, immense love that you have painted for me; if your heart is truly capable of feeling it; cast aside forever a thought inspired solely by jealousy and selfishness.
adequacy: Sab!" she continued with a full and firm voice, "if it is true that you love Carlota with that holy, immense love that you have described to me; if your heart is truly capable of feeling it; cast aside forever a thought inspired solely by jealousy and selfishness.

es: ¡Bárbaro!... ¿quién te da el derecho de arrancarla de sus ilusiones, de privarla de los momentos de felicidad que ellas proporcionarla?, ¿qué habrás logrado cuando la despiertes de ese sueño de amor, que es su única existencia?, ¿qué le darás en cambio de las esperanzas que le robes?
en: Barbarian!... who gives you the right to tear her from her illusions, to deprive her of the moments of happiness that they provide her? What will you have achieved when you awaken her from that dream of love, which is her only existence? What will you give her in exchange for the hopes that you steal from her?
draft: Barbarian!... who gives you the right to tear her from her illusions, to deprive her of the moments of happiness that they provide her? What will you have achieved when you awaken her from that dream of love, which is her only existence? What will you give her in exchange for the hopes that you steal from her?

es: ¡Oh!, desgraciado el hombre que anticipa a otro el terrible día del desengaño!
en: Oh, wretched is the man who anticipates for another the terrible day of disillusionment!"
draft: Oh, wretched is the man who anticipates for another the terrible day of disillusionment!"
adequacy: Oh, wretched is the man who anticipates for another the terrible day of disillusionment!"

es: Detúvose un momento y viendo que Sab la escuchaba inmóvil añadió con más dulzura:
en: She paused for a moment and, seeing that Sab was listening to her motionless, she added with more sweetness:
draft: She paused for a moment and, seeing that Sab was listening to her motionless, she added with more sweetness:
adequacy: She paused for a moment and, seeing that Sab was listening to her motionless, she added with more sweetness:

es: -Tu corazón es noble y generoso, si las pasiones le extravían un momento él debe volver más recto y grande.
en: "Your heart is noble and generous; if passions lead it astray for a moment, it must return more upright and great.
draft: "Your heart is noble and generous; if passions lead it astray for a moment, it must return more upright and great.
adequacy: "Your heart is noble and generous; if passions lead it astray for a moment, it must return more upright and great.

es: Al presente eres libre y rico: la suerte, justa esta vez, te ha dado los medios de elevar tu destino a la altura de tu alma.
en: At present you are free and rich: fate, just this time, has given you the means to raise your destiny to the height of your soul.
draft: At present you are free and rich: fate, just this time, has given you the means to raise your destiny to the height of your soul.
adequacy: At present you are free and rich: fate, just this time, has given you the means to raise your destiny to the height of your soul.

es: El bienhechor de Martina tiene oro para repartir entre los desgraciados, y la dicha de la virtud le aguarda a él mismo, al término de la senda que le abre la providencia.
en: The benefactor of Martina has gold to distribute among the wretched, and the happiness of virtue awaits him himself, at the end of the path that providence opens for him."
draft: The benefactor of Martina has gold to distribute among the wretched, and the happiness of virtue awaits him himself, at the end of the path that providence opens for him."
adequacy: The benefactor of Martina has gold to distribute among the wretched, and the happiness of virtue awaits him himself, at the end of the path that providence opens for him."

es: Sab miró a Teresa con ojos extraviados y como si saliese de un penoso sueño.

draft: Sab looked at Teresa with dazed eyes and as if he were emerging from a painful dream.
adequacy: Sab looked at Teresa with dazed eyes and as if he were emerging from a painful dream.

es: -¿Dónde estoy? -exclamó-, ¿qué hacéis aquí?, ¿ a qué habéis venido?
en: "Where am I?" he exclaimed, "what are you doing here? Why have you come?"
draft: "Where am I?" he exclaimed, "what are you doing here? Why have you come?"
adequacy: "Where am I?" he exclaimed, "what are you doing here? Why have you come?"

es: -A consolarte -respondió conmovida la doncella-.
en: "To console you," the young lady replied, moved.
draft: "To console you," the young lady replied, moved.
adequacy: "To console you," the young lady replied, moved.

es: ¡Sab!, querido Sab..., vuelve en ti.
en: "Sab! Dear Sab... come to your senses."
draft: "Sab! Dear Sab... come to your senses."
adequacy: "Sab! Dear Sab... come to your senses."

es: -¡Querido! -repitió él con despedazante sonrisa-: ¡querido!..., no, nunca lo he sido, nunca podré serlo..., ¿veis esta fuente, señora?, ¿qué os dice ella?, ¿no notáis este color opaco y siniestro?..., es la marca de mi raza maldecida...
en: "Dear!" he repeated with a heartbreaking smile: "dear!... no, I have never been, I will never be able to be... do you see this fountain, señora? What does it tell you? Do you not notice this opaque and sinister color?... it is the mark of my cursed race..."

adequacy: "And, nevertheless," he added, pressing Teresa's hands convulsively against his chest, "nevertheless, there was in this heart a fertile germ of great feelings."

es: Si mi destino no los hubiera sofocado, si la abyección del hombre físico no se hubiera opuesto constantemente al desarrollo del hombre moral, acaso hubiera yo sido grande y virtuoso.
en: "If my destiny had not stifled them, if the abjection of the physical man had not constantly opposed the development of the moral man, perhaps I would have been great and virtuous."
draft: "If my destiny had not stifled them, if the abjection of the physical man had not constantly opposed the development of the moral man, perhaps I would have been great and virtuous."
adequacy: "If my destiny had not stifled them, if the abjection of the physical man had not constantly opposed the development of the moral man, perhaps I would have been great and virtuous."

es: Esclavo he debido pensar como esclavo, porque el hombre sin dignidad ni derechos, no puede conservar sentimientos nobles.
en: "As a slave I have had to think like a slave, because the man without dignity or rights cannot preserve noble feelings."
draft: "As a slave I have had to think like a slave, because the man without dignity or rights cannot preserve noble feelings."
adequacy: "As a slave I have had to think like a slave, because the man without dignity or rights cannot preserve noble feelings."

es: ¡Teresa!, debéis despreciarme..., ¿por qué estáis aquí todavía?..., huid, señora, y dejadme morir.

draft: "Teresa! You must despise me... why are you still here?... flee, señora, and let me die."
adequacy: "Teresa! You must despise me... why are you still here?... flee, señora, and let me die."

es: -¡No! -exclamó ella inclinando su cabeza sobre la del mulato, arrodillado a sus pies-; no me apartaré de ti sin que me jures respetar tu vida.

draft: "No!" she exclaimed, bowing her head over that of the mulatto, who was kneeling at her feet; "I will not leave you without you swearing to me to respect your life."
adequacy: "No!" she exclaimed, bowing her head over that of the mulatto, who was kneeling at her feet; "I will not leave you without you swearing to me to respect your life."

es: Un sudor frío corría por la frente de Sab, y la opresión de su corazón embargaba su voz; sin embargo, a los dulces acentos de Teresa levantó a ella sus ojos, llenos de gratitud.
en: A cold sweat ran down Sab's forehead, and the oppression of his heart choked his voice; nevertheless, at the sweet accents of Teresa, he raised his eyes to her, filled with gratitude.
draft: A cold sweat ran down Sab's forehead, and the oppression of his heart choked his voice; nevertheless, at the sweet accents of Teresa, he raised his eyes to her, filled with gratitude.
adequacy: A cold sweat ran down Sab's forehead, and the oppression of his heart choked his voice; nevertheless, at the sweet accents of Teresa, he raised his eyes to her, filled with gratitude.

es: -¡Cuán buena sois! -la dijo-, pero ¿quién soy yo para que os intereséis por mi vida?..., ¡mi vida! ¿Sabéis vos lo que es mi vida?..., ¿a quién es necesaria?... Yo no tengo padre ni madre..., soy solo en el mundo: nadie llorará mi muerte.
en: "How good you are!" he said to her, "but who am I that you should take an interest in my life?... my life! Do you know what my life is?... to whom is it necessary?... I have neither father nor mother... I am alone in the world: no one will weep for my death."

es: No tengo tampoco una patria que defender, porque los esclavos no tienen patria; no tengo deberes que cumplir, porque los deberes del esclavo son los deberes de la bestia de carga, que anda mientras puede y se echa a tierra cuando ya no puede más.
en: I have no homeland to defend either, because slaves have no homeland; I have no duties to fulfill, because the duties of the slave are the duties of the beast of burden, which walks while it can and lies down on the ground when it can no longer go on.
draft: I do not have a homeland to defend either, because slaves have no homeland; I have no duties to fulfill, because the duties of the slave are the duties of the beast of burden, which walks while it can and throws itself to the ground when it can no longer go on.
adequacy: I have no homeland to defend either, because slaves have no homeland; I have no duties to fulfill, because the duties of the slave are the duties of the beast of burden, which walks while it can and lies down on the ground when it can no longer go on.

es: Si al menos los hombres blancos, que desechan de sus sociedades al que nació teñida la tez de un color diferente, le dejasen tranquilo en sus bosques, allá tendría patria y amores..., porque amaría a una mujer de su color, salvaje como él, y que como él no hubiera visto jamás otros climas ni otros hombres, ni conocido la ambición, ni admirado los talentos.
en: If at least white men, who cast out from their societies those born with skin dyed a different color, would leave him in peace in his forests, there he would have a homeland and loves... because he would love a woman of his color, wild like him, and who like him had never seen other climates or other men, nor known ambition, nor admired talents.

en: But, ah!, to the black man is refused what is granted to the ferocious beasts, to whom they equate him; because they are allowed to live among the mountains where they were born, and the black man is torn from his own.

en: A debased slave will bequeath as an inheritance to his children slavery and debasement, and those wretched children will ask in vain for the wild life of their parents.

es: En vano sentirán en su cabeza una fuerza pensadora, en vano en su pecho un corazón que palpite, «el poder y la voluntad», en vano un instinto, una convicción que les grite: «levantaos y marchad»; porque para ellos todos los caminos están cerrados, todas las esperanzas destruidas.
en: In vain will they feel in their head a thinking force, in vain in their chest a heart that beats, "the power and the will," in vain an instinct, a conviction that shouts to them: "rise up and march"; because for them all paths are closed, all hopes destroyed.

es: ¡Teresa!, esa es mi suerte.

adequacy: Teresa!, that is my lot.

en: "Leave these lands, leave them," exclaimed Teresa with energy; "poor young man, seek another sky, another climate, another existence..., seek also another love...; a wife worthy of your heart."

en: I am unworthy of you!; my love, this senseless love that devours me, began with my life and only with it can it end: the torments it causes me form my existence: I have nothing outside of it, I would be nothing if I ceased to love.

es: Y tú, mujer generosa, no conoces tú misma a lo que te obligas, no prevés los tormentos que te preparas.
en: And you, generous woman, you do not know yourself what you are binding yourself to, you do not foresee the torments you are preparing for yourself.

en: As for me, I have already loved, I have already lived... how many die without being able to say as much!, how many souls leave this world without having found an object in which they could employ their faculties of loving!

en: It does not matter that I have suffered, for I have loved Carlota, Carlota who is an angel!, Carlota, worthy object of all my worship! She has been more unfortunate than I: my love ennobles my heart and she..., ah, she has profaned hers!

en: But you are right, Teresa, it would be a barbarity to tell her: "that idol of your heart is a wretch incapable of understanding and loving you."

en: No!, never!, let her keep her illusions, which I will respect with religious veneration..., let her marry Enrique, and may she be happy!"

en: "But will she be!..., can she be when, after a few days of error and enthusiasm, she sees the veil of her illusions torn away, and finds herself united to a man she will have to despise?..."

en: And she will have to swear love and obedience to that man!, she will surrender to him her heart, her future, her entire destiny!..., she will make it a duty to respect him!, and he..., he will take her as a wife, like a piece of merchandise, out of calculation, out of convenience..., making a shameful speculation of the holiest bond, of the most solemn pledge! adequacy: And it was so, for a cold sweat ran from his forehead, and his wide-eyed gaze expressed the derangement of his reason.

en: It seemed to him that the earth was trembling beneath his feet and that the river, the trees, and the rocks were spinning in disorder around him.

en: The atmosphere was suffocating him and he felt a violent pain, a physical pain as if his heart were being torn apart by two iron claws, and an enormous mass of lead were being unloaded upon his head.

adequacy: Carlota as the wife of Enrique! She lavishing her caresses upon him!

en: She debasing her pure heart, her chaste charms with the coarse love of a wretch!
draft: She debasing her pure heart, her chaste charms with the coarse love of a wretch!
adequacy: She debasing her pure heart, her chaste charms with the coarse love of a miserable man!

en: This was his only thought, and this thought weighed upon his soul and upon each one of his limbs.
draft: This was his only thought, and this thought weighed upon his soul and upon each one of his limbs.
adequacy: This was his only thought, and this thought weighed upon his soul and upon each one of his limbs.

en: There was a moment when, frightened himself by what he was suffering, he doubted that the human constitution could withstand so much, and a confused and extravagant thought passed through his imagination.

en: It occurred to him that he had died, and that his soul was suffering those inconceivable torments that the wrath of God has prepared for the damned.

en: For there are sorrows whose frightening depth the sight of man cannot measure; the body is annihilated before them and only the soul, because it is infinite, can suffer and comprehend them.

en: His body seemed to be made of lead and, as happens in a nightmare, his efforts, exhausting his strength, did not succeed in moving him from that infernal rock upon which he seemed to be raised.

en: Inarticulate cries, which had nothing of the human accent, then issued from his chest, and Teresa saw him cast demented glances around him, and fix them at last upon her with frightening immobility.

en: The heart of Teresa was also breaking with pain at the sight of that wretch, and she wept over his tormented head, directing words of comfort to him.

en: Sab finally seemed to listen to her, because he sought with his trembling hand that of the maiden and, grasping it, pressed it against his breast, raising his burning eyes toward her; then, making a final and violent effort to rise, he fell at the feet of Teresa, as if all the muscles of his body had been broken.

en: "Wretched young man!" she thought, "who would remember your color upon seeing you love so much and suffer so much?"

en: "Young lady," he said to her with a faint voice, "are you still here? Have you not abandoned me like a cowardly soul, which is annihilated before the misfortune for which it should be so prepared?"
